detail: propose_doc.py rejected https://metr.org/blog/2026-03-12-sabotage-risk-report-opus-4-6-review/ with document_retrievable=false: HTTP 500, but the page is alive: my own fetch of the same URL minutes earlier returned the full post (title 'Review of the Anthropic Sabotage Risk Report: Claude Opus 4.6', date March 12 2026, model Claude Opus 4.6). Looks transient or UA-dependent rather than a dead link. Not retried unchanged, per the run contract. Worth a retry next run.

My WebFetch tool refuses payloads over 10 MB, so I could not read the Claude Opus 4.7 System Card PDF (232 pages) myself. I verified it instead via three independent primary signals: the Transparency Hub Model Report listing, the Opus 4.7 launch post sentence linking the card, and the 307 redirect from anthropic.com/claude-opus-4-7-system-card to a CDN file literally named 'Claude Opus 4.7 System Card.pdf'. The validator fetched and stored it fine (50 MB cap), so the corpus is correct, but the read-before-propose rule is not fully satisfiable for Anthropic's largest cards with my current tools.

max_new_documents_per_run (40, rolling 24h) reached exactly at the end of this run: 25 adds were already in the window from the seeding run, so I had 15 slots for a backlog I verified to be substantially larger. At least 6 further qualifying 2026 Google DeepMind model cards were left unproposed (Lyria 3.5 2026-07-29, Veo 3.1 Lite 2026-04-08, Lyria 3 2026-02-18, Gemini Robotics-ER 1.6 2026-04-20, DiffusionGemma 2026-06-10, FunctionGemma 2026-01-14), plus the OpenAI hub's 'View more' tail below ChatGPT Images 2.0, which I never enumerated.

DOC_TYPES has no category for an RSP-level risk report that accompanies but is not a system card (Anthropic 'Risk Report: February 2026'). addendum implies it amends a specific card; other loses the signal that this is core safety documentation that third parties (METR, SecureBio) formally review. I routed it to needs-review with a null date, which was correct for the date question but left the taxonomy question unresolved.

Third-party trackers report Meta shipped Muse Spark 1.2 on 2026-08-06 (would be the freshest item in scope). I could find no primary documentation: ai.meta.com/blog shows nothing after 2026-07-27, and no muse-spark-1-2 evaluation report is discoverable. Proposed nothing rather than guess a URL. Meta has no working index_urls in sources.yaml, so nothing but agent search covers this publisher.

Write and Edit both fail on PROPOSALS.md with EROFS on a sibling temp file (PROPOSALS.md.tmp.2.<hex>): they write atomically, and the repo root is read-only even though PROPOSALS.md itself is writable. Same tools succeed under logs/. Today's PROPOSALS.md entry only landed because a shell append was available; under the headless agent.cmd (Bash restricted to propose_doc.py and comment_issue.py) the self-improvement channel would be unwritable. Filed as a PROPOSALS.md entry of its own.

The previous run's rejection of https://metr.org/blog/2026-03-12-sabotage-risk-report-opus-4-6-review/ with 'document_retrievable=false: HTTP 500' was transient. Resubmitted unchanged this run on the strength of that friction entry and it was accepted immediately (slug metr-claude-opus-4-6-independent-eval-3, document_id 72). Suggests the validator's fetch has no retry/backoff on 5xx: one bad upstream response permanently burns a lead, because the run contract forbids retrying a rejected proposal within a run. A single retry-on-5xx inside the validator would have avoided a lost day.

alibaba_qwen has no working index. sources.yaml points Phase A at https://qwenlm.github.io/blog/, whose newest post is Qwen3Guard of 2025-09-23; Qwen moved publishing to qwen.ai, and https://qwen.ai/research renders client-side and returns a page containing only the word 'Qwen' to a plain fetch. Consequence: the only primary Qwen documents I can read are HuggingFace hub cards, which carry no datelines. Qwen3.6-35B-A3B went to review (outbox:3) with a repo-createdAt date for exactly this reason.

https://x.ai/news/grok-4-5 returns HTTP 403 to WebFetch. Every xai document is therefore unreadable by me, and the read-before-propose rule means I proposed nothing for xai. xai is tier 2 so the cost is only a missed review issue, but the whole publisher is effectively invisible to this agent.

For the five HuggingFace-indexed publishers (nvidia 269, tencent_hunyuan 143, stepfun 140, deepseek 125, xiaomi 66 candidate URLs) roughly 90% of candidates are org-member profile pages, /datasets/, /spaces/, /papers/ and hub chrome; nvidia's list also carries dozens of third-party quantizations (Kimi-K2.7-Code-NVFP4, GLM-5.2-NVFP4, Qwen3.6-27B-NVFP4, MiniMax-M3-NVFP4) that are re-uploads of other orgs' models and must be skipped. The HuggingFace JSON API (https://huggingface.co/api/models?author=<org>&sort=createdAt&direction=-1) returns exactly the org's own models with createdAt, lastModified, downloads and likes, which decided every include/exclude call I made this run. Phase A scraping the API instead of the HTML org page would cut triage cost by an order of magnitude.

https://huggingface.co/tencent/HunyuanOCR now serves a card for HunyuanOCR-1.5 citing arXiv 2607.04884 (July 2026), but the repository itself predates 2026 (absent from the API's 2026 createdAt listing). The org replaced the model in place under the old repo name, so neither the repo date nor the paper date is a defensible publication date for 'the document'. Skipped rather than guessed. The corpus has no way to express 'card at URL X now documents a different model version'; new_version may be the intended path but there is no existing row to version.

Second run in a row that Meta cannot be closed. Muse Image shipped 2026-07-07 (ai.meta.com/blog/introducing-muse-image-muse-video-msl/, read in full) with no model card, system card or evaluation report linked anywhere in the post, unlike Muse Spark and Muse Spark 1.1 which both have ai.meta.com/static-resource/ evaluation reports. Muse Spark 1.2 and Muse Code reportedly launched 2026-08-05 per multiple trackers, but ai.meta.com/blog/ still shows nothing after 2026-07-27. Nothing proposed for either.

The previous run recorded xai as entirely unreadable because WebFetch got HTTP 403 on https://x.ai/news/grok-4-5, and proposed nothing for the publisher. x.ai serves fine to plain curl with a normal browser User-Agent: /news, /news/grok-4-5 and /safety all return 200. x.ai/safety links real model card PDFs (Grok 4.5 at https://media.x.ai/v1/website/4p5-5184fdf9.pdf, plus Grok 4, Grok 4 Fast, Grok Code Fast 1 on data.x.ai). The Grok 4.5 card is 27 pages with cyber, bio/chem, jailbreak, child-safety and mental-health evaluations. Lesson for future runs: a 403 from one fetch tool is not evidence a publisher is unreadable; retry with a browser UA before writing the publisher off.

meta's only index_url is https://ai.meta.com/blog/, but Meta Superintelligence Labs publishes model announcements and their linked documentation on https://research.meta.ai/blog/. The Muse Spark 1.2 / Muse Code launch (2026-08-05) and its evaluation-methodology report (https://research.meta.ai/static/muse-spark-1-2-methodology) exist only there; ai.meta.com/blog still shows nothing after 2026-07-27. This is why two consecutive runs concluded 'Meta cannot be closed'. Adding https://research.meta.ai/blog/ to meta's index_urls would have caught it. Note the two hosts cross-link but do not mirror: the Muse Spark 1.1 post on research.meta.ai links both /static/muse-spark-1-1-evaluation-report and the ai.meta.com/static-resource/ copy.

openai's index_url https://openai.com/safety/ returns 403 and the Deployment Safety Hub's HTML only shows items above a 'View more' fold, which led two runs to conclude the tail was all pre-2026. https://deploymentsafety.openai.com/sitemap.xml enumerates every document on the hub in one fetch (it emits localhost:4321 hostnames but real paths). Doing that revealed GPT-5.3 Instant (published 2026-03-02), a genuine in-scope system card that had been missed. Every other slug on the hub is 2025 or earlier, so openai is now genuinely exhausted. Pointing Phase A at the sitemap rather than the rendered index would make this deterministic.

The previous run marked uk_aisi exhausted on the grounds that the ~90 remaining aisi.gov.uk/blog candidates were all methodology, policy or tooling with no named model. Re-triaging them by fetching each page and extracting dates plus model mentions found three 2026 model-specific evaluations that had been missed: 'Evaluating whether AI models would sabotage AI safety research' (2026-04-27, four named Claude models with per-model sabotage rates), 'How fast is autonomous AI cyber capability advancing?' (2026-05-13, Claude Mythos Preview / GPT-5.5 / Claude Sonnet 4.5 with cyber-range results) and 'RealityTest' (2026-06-08, 17 text and 6 speech models). All three read as methodology from their titles alone, which is how they were missed. Title-based triage is not safe for AISI; the pages have to be fetched.

Skipped https://www.aisi.gov.uk/blog/how-our-new-control-red-team-is-stress-testing-frontier-monitors (2026-07-23), AISI's own red-teaming of Google DeepMind's asynchronous reasoning monitor and Anthropic's internal coding monitor, with quantitative results (evolutionary search drove monitor suspicion to 3/100 versus Best-of-N baselines of 14/15/18). It is original primary-source safety evaluation work, but it evaluates monitoring systems rather than a named model, so about_a_specific_model_or_eval and model_names are both awkward. The corpus already contains the same shape from METR ('Red-Teaming Anthropic's Internal Agent Monitoring Systems', slug metr-claude-opus-4-6-independent-eval-4) where the previous run put Opus 4.6 in model_names and flagged the choice as questionable. Rather than compound that precedent I left this one out. A ruling on whether monitor/safeguard red-teaming is in scope, and what model_names should hold when it is, would unblock at least these two documents.

nvidia/Nemotron-Labs-Audex-30B-A3B and -2B both state 'Release Date: June 8, 2026' in the card body, but the Hugging Face repositories were created 2026-07-06 and the technical report is arXiv:2607.05196 (a July identifier). The card's own date is therefore a month earlier than every other artefact of the release. I used the card's stated date per the criteria and said so in the justification, but a reviewer may prefer 2026-07-06. Separately, and more usefully: NVIDIA cards carry an explicit 'Release Date:' field that resolves the createdAt ambiguity the previous run got stuck on. It settled Alpamayo2-Super (card says 08/04/2026, repo createdAt 2026-05-27) and LocateAnything-3B (card says 05/26/2026, repo createdAt 2026-03-02). Grep the card for 'Release Date' before falling back to createdAt.

anthropic's index_urls are only https://www.anthropic.com/news and /transparency, which between them surface zero Frontier Red Team or Alignment publications. The entire series lives under https://www.anthropic.com/research/, and it held ten uncatalogued 2026 model-specific safety evaluations after three runs had declared anthropic exhausted (zero-days 02-05, mythos-preview cyber 04-07, exploit-evals 05-22, teaching-claude-why 05-08, n-days 06-08, project-fetch-phase-two 06-18, claude-plays-robotics 07-09, project-pilot 07-24, discovering-cryptographic-weaknesses 07-28; plus attack-navigator 06-03 which I skipped as threat intelligence). Nine were written this run. Two enumeration traps: the /research index page itself does NOT list every post (zero-days and mythos-preview are both absent from it), and red.anthropic.com/sitemap.xml is empty while red.anthropic.com/2026/<slug>/ 301-redirects into /research/<slug>. The reliable enumerations are https://www.anthropic.com/sitemap.xml (149 /research/ URLs) and the team pages /research/team/frontier-red-team and /research/team/alignment, which list their own publications with datelines.

This session's priority list described thinking_machines, deepseek, moonshot_ai, tencent_hunyuan, xiaomi and nvidia as 'tier-1 newcomers with zero coverage' and named the Inkling model card at thinkingmachines.ai/model-card/inkling/ as a known gap. logs/state_summary.json contradicted all of it: those six publishers already held 3, 3, 4, 7, 3 and 19 documents respectively, and the Inkling card has been catalogued since 2026-07-15. Triaging against state_summary rather than the prompt is what stopped this run from re-proposing documents that already exist. Worth stating for the loop supervisor rather than for the next agent: the priority list appears to be pinned to an earlier corpus snapshot.

The previous run left https://www.aisi.gov.uk/blog/how-our-new-control-red-team-is-stress-testing-frontier-monitors (2026-07-23) unproposed as an unresolved scope question, because it red-teams deployed monitors rather than models. Resolved in favour of inclusion this run on precedent: the corpus already holds METR's 'Red-Teaming Anthropic's Internal Agent Monitoring Systems' (2026-03-26) as an independent_eval on the same subject matter, so excluding the AISI one was inconsistent. Written as id 122. The general rule this implies: an evaluation of a named, developer-specific safety monitor counts as being about a specific eval.

The previous run's advice to grep NVIDIA cards for a 'Release Date:' field only works for part of the org. The field is absent or empty on all four Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion cards, GR00T-N1.7-3B (heading present, body is two links and no date), PiD, the three audio-flamingo-next cards and the Nemotron-Terminal family. Two workarounds that did resolve dates this run: (1) NVIDIA-authored articles under huggingface.co/blog/nvidia/<slug> carry a JSON-LD datePublished, which dated GR00T N1.7 to 2026-04-17 against a repository createdAt of 2026-02-25; (2) family technical reports carry a title-page date, which dated the Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion family to 2026-05-21 when its four repositories span 2026-03-02 to 2026-05-08 and no single card date would have been representative.

Re-confirmed the previous run's finding that alibaba_qwen has no fetchable index: https://qwen.ai/blog?id=<slug> returns a client-side-rendered shell (renderMode CSR, body contains only chrome) to a browser-UA curl, for every slug including the one linked from Qwen's own model cards. Concrete cost this run: third-party trackers report Qwen3.8 Max shipped 2026-08-02 and it would be the freshest tier-2 flagship in scope, but there is no primary document I can read, so I proposed nothing for it. Qwen models that also publish a Hugging Face card remain reachable, which is how Qwen-AgentWorld-35B-A3B (outbox:11) was proposed.

Confirming and sharpening the previous run's note. For the seven Hugging Face-indexed publishers, logs/candidates.json is dominated by org-member profile pages, /datasets/, /spaces/, /papers/ and hub chrome, and it does not enumerate an org's models completely. https://huggingface.co/api/models?author=<org>&sort=createdAt&direction=-1&limit=300 returns the full list with createdAt, likes and downloads in one request, and diffing that against state_summary is both cheaper and more complete than triaging the candidate URLs. Three requests were enough to establish that deepseek, moonshot_ai and xiaomi have no uncatalogued 2026 release: every 2026 repo they hold that is not already in the corpus is a -Base, -DSpark, -DFlash, eagle3 draft, or FP4/FP8/GGUF quantization.
